152	def compute_fourin_mapping_indices(mode_table, *, nper, lsx):
153	    """Return TERPSICHORE ``FOURIN`` sum/difference lookup indices."""
154	
155	    lmns = mode_table.size
156	    ms = np.asarray(mode_table.m, dtype=int)
157	    ns = np.asarray(mode_table.n, dtype=int)
158	    lmd = np.zeros((lmns, lmns), dtype=int)
159	    lmp = np.zeros((lmns, lmns), dtype=int)
160	    ndd = np.zeros((lmns, lmns), dtype=int)
161	    ndp = np.zeros((lmns, lmns), dtype=int)
162	    ld = np.zeros((lmns, lmns), dtype=int)
163	    lp = np.zeros((lmns, lmns), dtype=int)
164	    for lc in range(lmns):
165	        for lr in range(lmns):
166	            diff_n = int(ns[lc] - ns[lr])
167	            sum_n = int(ns[lc] + ns[lr])
168	            lmd[lc, lr] = min(1, abs(_fortran_mod(diff_n, nper)))
169	            lmp[lc, lr] = min(1, abs(_fortran_mod(sum_n, nper)))
170	            ndd[lc, lr] = int(diff_n / nper)
171	            ndp[lc, lr] = int(sum_n / nper)
172	            ld[lc, lr] = _lsx_lookup(lsx, int(ms[lc] - ms[lr]), ndd[lc, lr], lmd[lc, lr])
173	            lp[lc, lr] = _lsx_lookup(lsx, int(ms[lc] + ms[lr]), ndp[lc, lr], lmp[lc, lr])
174	    return {"lmd": lmd, "lmp": lmp, "ndd": ndd, "ndp": ndp, "ld": ld, "lp": lp}

176	def map_fourin_integrals_to_coefficients(
177	    *,
178	    cna,
179	    cnb,
180	    mode_table,
181	    nper,
182	    lsx,
183	    dtdp,
184	    cospar,
185	    cospr2,
186	    ftp,
187	    fpp,
188	    ftpp,
189	    fppp,
190	    ci,
191	    cj,
192	    modelk=0,
193	    s_centers=None,
194	    cip=None,
195	    cjp=None,
196	    pp=None,
197	    fixed_boundary=True,
198	    igreen=0,
199	):
200	    """Map pre-integrated FOURIN ``cna``/``cnb`` arrays to ``c0..c11``."""
201	
202	    cna = np.asarray(cna, dtype=float)
203	    cnb = np.asarray(cnb, dtype=float)
204	    if cna.shape != cnb.shape or cna.ndim != 3:
205	        raise ValueError("cna and cnb must be rank-3 arrays with identical shape.")
206	    if cna.shape[0] < 7:
207	        raise ValueError("cna/cnb first dimension must include indices 1..6.")
208	    lmns = mode_table.size
209	    intervals = cna.shape[2]
210	    shape = (lmns, lmns, intervals)
211	    coeffs = {name: np.zeros(shape) for name in ALL_COEFFICIENTS}
212	    indices = compute_fourin_mapping_indices(mode_table, nper=nper, lsx=lsx)
213	    ld = indices["ld"]
214	    lp = indices["lp"]
215	    for interval in range(intervals):
216	        coeffs["c2"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
217	            cna[1, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[1, lp, interval]
218	        )
219	        coeffs["c6"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
220	            cna[2, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[2, lp, interval]
221	        )
222	        coeffs["c7"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
223	            cna[3, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[3, lp, interval]
224	        )
225	        coeffs["c5"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
226	            cna[4, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[4, lp, interval]
227	        )
228	        coeffs["c0"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
229	            cna[6, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[6, lp, interval]
230	        )
231	        coeffs["c1"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
232	            cnb[1, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[1, lp, interval]
233	        )
234	        coeffs["c3"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
235	            cnb[2, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[2, lp, interval]
236	        )
237	        coeffs["c4"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
238	            cnb[3, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[3, lp, interval]
239	        )
240	        if modelk > 1:
241	            coeffs["c8"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
242	                cnb[5, ld, interval] - cospar * cnb[5, lp, interval]
243	            )
244	            coeffs["c10"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
245	                cnb[4, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[4, lp, interval]
246	            )
247	            coeffs["c11"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
248	                cnb[6, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[6, lp, interval]
249	            )
250	        else:
251	            coeffs["c8"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
252	                cna[5, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[5, lp, interval]
253	            )
254	            coeffs["c11"][:, :, interval] = 0.0
255	            ftp_i = np.asarray(ftp, dtype=float)[interval]
256	            coeffs["c10"][:, :, interval] = (
257	                coeffs["c8"][:, :, interval] + dtdp * cospr2 * cna[5, lp, interval]
258	            ) / (4.0 * ftp_i * ftp_i)
259	    ftp_arr = np.asarray(ftp, dtype=float)
260	    fpp_arr = np.asarray(fpp, dtype=float)
261	    ftpp_arr = np.asarray(ftpp, dtype=float)
262	    fppp_arr = np.asarray(fppp, dtype=float)
263	    ci_arr = np.asarray(ci, dtype=float)
264	    cj_arr = np.asarray(cj, dtype=float)
265	    ql = np.asarray(mode_table.ql, dtype=float)
266	    ms = np.asarray(mode_table.m, dtype=float)
267	    ns = np.asarray(mode_table.n, dtype=float)
268	    if s_centers is None:
269	        s_centers_arr = (np.arange(intervals, dtype=float) + 0.5) / intervals
270	    else:
271	        s_centers_arr = np.asarray(s_centers, dtype=float)
272	        if s_centers_arr.shape != (intervals,):
273	            raise ValueError(f"s_centers must have shape {(intervals,)}, got {s_centers_arr.shape}.")
274	    ql_lc = ql[:, None]
275	    ql_lr = ql[None, :]
276	    for interval in range(intervals):
277	        si = s_centers_arr[interval]
278	        t0 = fpp_arr[interval] * ftpp_arr[interval] - ftp_arr[interval] * fppp_arr[interval]
279	        sqgbsq = cj_arr[interval] * fpp_arr[interval] - ci_arr[interval] * ftp_arr[interval]
280	        if abs(sqgbsq) < 1e-14:
281	            raise ValueError("FOURIN mapping encountered near-zero SQGBSQ denominator.")
282	        t2 = t0 / sqgbsq
283	        t3 = t0 * t0 / sqgbsq
284	        t4 = (cj_arr[interval] * fppp_arr[interval] - ci_arr[interval] * ftpp_arr[interval]) / sqgbsq
285	        pmn = (ms * fpp_arr[interval] - ns * ftp_arr[interval])[:, None]
286	        rmn = (ms * fpp_arr[interval] - ns * ftp_arr[interval])[None, :]
287	        coeffs["c9"][:, :, interval] = (
288	            coeffs["c7"][:, :, interval]
289	            + t0 * coeffs["c5"][:, :, interval]
290	            + t3 * coeffs["c6"][:, :, interval]
291	            + (t4 - ql_lc / si)
292	            * (t4 - ql_lr / si)
293	            * sqgbsq
294	            * coeffs["c0"][:, :, interval]
295	            + (t4 - (ql_lc + ql_lr) / si) * coeffs["c2"][:, :, interval]
296	            + pmn * rmn * coeffs["c3"][:, :, interval]
297	            - rmn
298	            * (
299	                t2 * coeffs["c4"][:, :, interval]
300	                + (t4 - ql_lc / si) * coeffs["c1"][:, :, interval]
301	            )
302	            - pmn
303	            * (
304	                t2 * coeffs["c4"][:, :, interval].T
305	                + (t4 - ql_lr / si) * coeffs["c1"][:, :, interval].T
306	            )
307	        )
308	    profiles = {
309	        "ftp": ftp_arr,
310	        "fpp": fpp_arr,
311	        "ftpp": ftpp_arr,
312	        "fppp": fppp_arr,
313	        "ci": ci_arr,
314	        "cj": cj_arr,
315	    }
316	    coeff_data = TerpsichoreCoefficientData(
317	        coefficients=coeffs,
318	        profiles=profiles,
319	        fixed_boundary=fixed_boundary,
320	        igreen=igreen,
321	    )
322	    return coeff_data

331	def compute_fourin_grid_functions(*, grid_data, profiles, interval, modelk=0):
332	    """Compute FOURIN plasma grid functions ``A0..A11`` for one interval.
333	
334	    This ports the plasma branches of Fortran ``FOURIN`` for reduced and
335	    physical kinetic energy models: NI (``modelk`` 0/2) and KO (``modelk`` 1/3).
336	    """
337	
338	    if modelk not in {0, 1, 2, 3}:
339	        raise ValueError("modelk must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3.")
340	    sigmab = _grid_array(grid_data, "sigmab")[:, interval]
341	    sigbs = _grid_array(grid_data, "sigbs")[:, interval]
342	    gstl = _grid_array(grid_data, "gstl")[:, interval]
343	    gssl = _grid_array(grid_data, "gssl")[:, interval]
344	    gssu = _grid_array(grid_data, "gssu")[:, interval]
345	    bjac = _grid_array(grid_data, "bjac")[:, interval]
346	    bjacs = _grid_array(grid_data, "bjacs")[:, interval]
347	    parjp = _grid_array(grid_data, "parjp")[:, interval]
348	    gspl = _grid_array(grid_data, "gspl")[:, interval] if "gspl" in grid_data else None
349	    ftp = np.asarray(profiles["ftp"], dtype=float)[interval]
350	    fpp = np.asarray(profiles["fpp"], dtype=float)[interval]
351	    ftpp = np.asarray(profiles.get("ftpp", np.zeros_like(profiles["ftp"])), dtype=float)[interval]
352	    fppp = np.asarray(profiles.get("fppp", np.zeros_like(profiles["ftp"])), dtype=float)[interval]
353	    ci = np.asarray(profiles["ci"], dtype=float)[interval]
354	    cj = np.asarray(profiles["cj"], dtype=float)[interval]
355	    pp = np.asarray(profiles["pp"], dtype=float)[interval]
356	    sqgbsq = cj * fpp - ci * ftp
357	    if abs(ftp) < 1e-14:
358	        raise ValueError("FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero ftp denominator.")
359	    if abs(sqgbsq) < 1e-14:
360	        raise ValueError("FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero SQGBSQ denominator.")
361	    if np.any(np.abs(sigmab) < 1e-14):
362	        raise ValueError("FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero sigmab denominator.")
363	    gsplm = (sigbs / sigmab - fpp * gstl) / ftp
364	    if modelk in {1, 3}:
365	        taub = _grid_array(grid_data, "taub")[:, interval]
366	        gparp = _grid_array(grid_data, "gparp")[:, interval]
367	        gperp = _grid_array(grid_data, "gperp")[:, interval]
368	        parkur = _grid_array(grid_data, "parkur")[:, interval]
369	        pphotj = _grid_array(grid_data, "pphotj")[:, interval]
370	        if np.any(np.abs(taub) < 1e-14):
371	            raise ValueError("KO FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero taub denominator.")
372	        sigtau = sigmab / taub
373	        t8 = cj * fppp - ci * ftpp
374	        if "cjp" in profiles and "cip" in profiles:
375	            t8 = t8 + np.asarray(profiles["cjp"], dtype=float)[interval] * fpp - np.asarray(profiles["cip"], dtype=float)[interval] * ftp
376	        pgradt = bjac * pp * (1.0 + sigtau) + gparp + sigtau * gperp
377	        funcs = {
378	            "a0": 1.0 / sigtau,
379	            "a1": sigbs / sigtau,
380	            "a2": pp * bjac + gperp,
381	            "a3": sigmab * gssl - (1.0 - 1.0 / sigtau) * sigbs * sigbs / sqgbsq,
382	            "a4": sigmab * (ci * gstl + cj * gsplm),
383	            "a5": parkur,
384	            "a6": gssu,
385	            "a7": (pgradt * bjacs) / (1.0 + sigtau)
386	            - (((gparp - gperp) * (pgradt + t8)) / (1.0 + sigtau) + sigbs * pphotj)
387	            / sqgbsq,
388	        }
389	    else:
390	        funcs = {
391	            "a0": 1.0 / sigmab,
392	            "a1": sigbs / sigmab,
393	            "a2": pp * bjac,
394	            "a3": gssl,
395	            "a4": ci * gstl + cj * gsplm,
396	            "a5": parjp,
397	            "a6": gssu / sigmab,
398	            "a7": pp * bjac * bjacs,
399	        }
400	    if modelk in {2, 3}:
401	        if gspl is None:
402	            raise ValueError("physical kinetic energy models require grid_data['gspl'] for A11.")
403	        funcs["a8"] = bjac * bjac * gssl
404	        funcs["a10"] = bjac * bjac * funcs["a6"] / sqgbsq
405	        funcs["a11"] = -bjac * bjac * (ci * gstl + cj * gspl) / sqgbsq
406	    else:
407	        zeros = np.zeros_like(sigmab)
408	        funcs["a8"] = zeros
409	        funcs["a10"] = zeros
410	        funcs["a11"] = zeros
411	    return funcs

414	def accumulate_fourin_integrals_from_grid_functions(*, functions, tsc, tss, bjac):
415	    """Accumulate one-interval ``cna``/``cnb`` from FOURIN grid functions.
416	
417	    This ports the visible summation loops after ``A0..A11`` construction in
418	    Fortran ``FOURIN``.  The trigonometric tables are expected in TERPSICHORE's
419	    ``(lss, njk)`` layout.
420	    """
421	
422	    tsc = np.asarray(tsc, dtype=float)
423	    tss = np.asarray(tss, dtype=float)
424	    bjac = np.asarray(bjac, dtype=float)
425	    if tsc.shape != tss.shape:
426	        raise ValueError("tsc and tss must have the same shape.")
427	    if bjac.shape != (tsc.shape[1],):
428	        raise ValueError("bjac must have shape (njk,).")
429	    lss_with_sentinel = tsc.shape[0]
430	    cna = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel))
431	    cnb = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel))
432	    cna[1] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a2"], dtype=float)
433	    cna[2] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a6"], dtype=float)
434	    cna[3] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a7"], dtype=float)
435	    cna[4] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a5"], dtype=float)
436	    cna[5] = tsc @ bjac
437	    cna[6] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a0"], dtype=float)
438	    cnb[1] = tss @ np.asarray(functions["a1"], dtype=float)
439	    cnb[3] = tss @ np.asarray(functions["a4"], dtype=float)
440	    cnb[4] = tss @ np.asarray(functions["a10"], dtype=float)
441	    cnb[2] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a3"], dtype=float)
442	    cnb[5] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a8"], dtype=float)
443	    cnb[6] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a11"], dtype=float)
444	    return cna, cnb

451	    """Compute raw FOURIN ``cna``/``cnb`` integral arrays from grid data."""

473	def compute_fourin_vacuum_integral_arrays_from_grid(*, vacuum_grid_data, trig_table):
474	    """Compute vacuum-domain raw ``cna``/``cnb`` arrays for TERPSICHORE ``FOURIN``.
475	
476	    The vacuum branch requires ``gppl``, ``gtpl``, ``gttl``, ``gstl``, ``gssl``
477	    and ``gssu`` on pseudo-vacuum intervals ``ni+1..nvi``. Callers must provide
478	    the complete metric terms from strict vacuum geometry reconstruction.
479	    """
480	
481	    required = ("gppl", "gtpl", "gttl", "gstl", "gssl", "gssu")
482	    missing = [name for name in required if vacuum_grid_data.get(name) is None]
483	    if missing:
484	        raise ValueError(
485	            "vacuum FOURIN requires metric arrays "
486	            + ", ".join(required)
487	            + f"; missing {tuple(missing)}"
488	        )
489	    arrays = {name: np.asarray(vacuum_grid_data[name], dtype=float) for name in required}
490	    shapes = {name: value.shape for name, value in arrays.items()}
491	    if len(set(shapes.values())) != 1:
492	        raise ValueError(f"vacuum metric arrays must have identical shapes, got {shapes}")
493	    points, intervals = next(iter(shapes.values()))
494	    if trig_table.tsc.shape[1] != points or trig_table.tss.shape[1] != points:
495	        raise ValueError("vacuum metric point count must match trigonometric tables.")
496	    lss_with_sentinel = trig_table.lss + 1
497	    cna = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel, intervals))
498	    cnb = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel, intervals))
499	    cna[1] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gppl"]
500	    cna[2] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gtpl"]
501	    cna[3] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gttl"]
502	    cnb[1] = trig_table.tss @ arrays["gstl"]
503	    cnb[2] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gssl"]
504	    cnb[3] = trig_table.tss @ arrays["gssu"]
505	    return cna, cnb

"""DESC equilibrium adapters for TERPSICHORE-native stability analysis."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np

from desc.grid import LinearGrid

from .options import TerpsichoreOptions
from .radial import TerpsichoreRadialGrid
from .vacuum import build_vacmet_inputs, vacmet_boundary_from_geometry


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TerpsichoreEquilibriumData:
    """Equilibrium quantities needed by the TERPSICHORE migration layer."""

    grid: object
    radial_grid: TerpsichoreRadialGrid
    data: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    nfp: int = 1
    sym: bool | str = False
    source: str = "desc"
    equilibrium: object | None = None

    def get(self, name, default=None):
        return self.data.get(name, default)


def _safe_compute(eq, names, grid):
    """Compute DESC quantities together, with a compatibility fallback."""

    names = tuple(names)
    data = {name: None for name in names}
    try:
        computed = eq.compute(list(names), grid=grid)
    except Exception:
        computed = None
    if computed is not None:
        for name in names:
            data[name] = computed.get(name)
        return data
    for name in names:
        try:
            data[name] = eq.compute(name, grid=grid)[name]
        except Exception:
            pass
    return data


def from_desc_equilibrium(eq, grid=None, options=None):
    """Convert a DESC ``Equilibrium`` into TERPSICHORE migration data.

    This adapter intentionally gathers geometry and equilibrium quantities without
    changing DESC's compute workflow. The originating equilibrium lets the
    native TERPSICHORE layer evaluate its own half-grid Boozer projection later.
    """

    options = TerpsichoreOptions() if options is None else options
    radial_grid = TerpsichoreRadialGrid.uniform(
        surfs=options.surfs,
        ivac=options.vacuum.ivac,
        dsvac=options.vacuum.dsvac,
    )
    if grid is None:
        rho = np.sqrt(radial_grid.s_nodes[: radial_grid.ni + 1])
        grid = LinearGrid(
            rho=rho,
            M=getattr(eq, "M_grid", getattr(eq, "M", 8)),
            N=getattr(eq, "N_grid", getattr(eq, "N", 8)),
            NFP=getattr(eq, "NFP", 1),
            sym=getattr(eq, "sym", False),
        )
    quantity_names = [
        "R",
        "R_r",
        "R_t",
        "R_z",
        "Z",
        "Z_r",
        "Z_t",
        "Z_z",
        "phi",
        "phi_r",
        "phi_t",
        "phi_z",
        "lambda",
        "sqrt(g)",
        "|B|",
        "|B|^2",
        "B^rho",
        "B^theta",
        "B^zeta",
        "p",
        "p_r",
        "psi_r",
        "iota",
        "current",
        "I",
        "I_r",
        "G",
        "G_r",
        "nu",
        "nu_t",
        "nu_z",
        "theta_PEST",
        "theta_PEST_t",
        "theta_PEST_z",
        "theta_B",
        "zeta_B",
        "sqrt(g)_Boozer",
        "sqrt(g)_Boozer_DESC",
        "g_rr",
        "g_rt",
        "g_rz",
        "g_tt",
        "g_tz",
        "g_zz",
    ]
    data = _safe_compute(eq, quantity_names, grid)
    return TerpsichoreEquilibriumData(
        grid=grid,
        radial_grid=radial_grid,
        data=data,
        nfp=getattr(eq, "NFP", 1),
        sym=getattr(eq, "sym", False),
        equilibrium=eq,
    )

def vacmet_inputs_from_equilibrium_data(
    equilibrium_data,
    *,
    wall=None,
    wall_scale=1.0,
    nowall=1,
    radial_index=-1,
):
    """Build VACMET inputs from ``TerpsichoreEquilibriumData`` geometry fields.

    This bridges the DESC/DESC-like geometry adapter to the native VACMET stage.
    It expects real-space geometry and derivatives in ``equilibrium_data.data``;
    DESC ``*_r/*_t/*_z`` derivative names are mapped onto TERPSICHORE
    ``*_s/*_theta/*_zeta`` aliases consumed by ``vacmet_boundary_from_geometry``.
    """

    radial_grid = equilibrium_data.radial_grid
    data = dict(equilibrium_data.data)
    geometry = {
        "R": data.get("R"),
        "Z": data.get("Z"),
        "phi": data.get("phi"),
        "Rs": data.get("Rs", data.get("R_s", data.get("R_r"))),
        "Rt": data.get("Rt", data.get("R_theta", data.get("R_t"))),
        "Rp": data.get("Rp", data.get("R_zeta", data.get("R_z"))),
        "Zs": data.get("Zs", data.get("Z_s", data.get("Z_r"))),
        "Zt": data.get("Zt", data.get("Z_theta", data.get("Z_t"))),
        "Zp": data.get("Zp", data.get("Z_zeta", data.get("Z_z"))),
        "phis": data.get("phis", data.get("phi_s", data.get("phi_r"))),
        "phit": data.get("phit", data.get("phi_theta", data.get("phi_t"))),
        "phip": data.get("phip", data.get("phi_zeta", data.get("phi_z"))),
        "Rst": data.get("Rst", data.get("R_st")),
        "Rsp": data.get("Rsp", data.get("R_sp")),
        "Zst": data.get("Zst", data.get("Z_st")),
        "Zsp": data.get("Zsp", data.get("Z_sp")),
        "phist": data.get("phist", data.get("phi_st")),
        "phisp": data.get("phisp", data.get("phi_sp")),
    }
    boundary = vacmet_boundary_from_geometry(geometry, radial_index=radial_index)
    dsvac = radial_grid.s_nodes[radial_grid.ni + radial_grid.ivac] - 1.0 if radial_grid.ivac else 0.0
    dsvac = float(data.get("dsvac", dsvac))
    pvac = float(data.get("pvac", 1.0))
    qvac = float(data.get("qvac", 1.0))
    tor = data.get("tor")
    return build_vacmet_inputs(
        s_nodes=radial_grid.s_nodes,
        ni=radial_grid.ni,
        ivac=radial_grid.ivac,
        dsvac=dsvac,
        pvac=pvac,
        qvac=qvac,
        nowall=nowall,
        boundary=boundary,
        wall=wall,
        wall_scale=wall_scale,
        tor=tor,
    )

"""Radial mesh objects for TERPSICHORE stability analysis."""

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TerpsichoreRadialGrid:
    """TERPSICHORE-style radial grid in normalized toroidal flux ``s``."""

    s_nodes: np.ndarray
    ni: int
    ivac: int = 0

    def __post_init__(self):
        s_nodes = np.asarray(self.s_nodes, dtype=float)
        if s_nodes.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError("s_nodes must be one-dimensional.")
        if s_nodes.size != self.ni + self.ivac + 1:
            raise ValueError("s_nodes length must equal ni + ivac + 1.")
        if self.ni < 1:
            raise ValueError("ni must be positive.")
        if self.ivac < 0:
            raise ValueError("ivac must be non-negative.")
        if np.any(np.diff(s_nodes) <= 0):
            raise ValueError("s_nodes must be strictly increasing.")
        if not np.isclose(s_nodes[0], 0.0):
            raise ValueError("s_nodes must start at 0.")
        if not np.isclose(s_nodes[self.ni], 1.0):
            raise ValueError("plasma boundary s_nodes[ni] must be 1.")
        object.__setattr__(self, "s_nodes", s_nodes)

    @property
    def n_intervals(self):
        return self.ni + self.ivac

    @property
    def centers(self):
        return 0.5 * (self.s_nodes[1:] + self.s_nodes[:-1])

    @property
    def ds(self):
        return np.diff(self.s_nodes)

    @property
    def plasma_slice(self):
        return slice(0, self.ni)

    @property
    def vacuum_slice(self):
        return slice(self.ni, self.ni + self.ivac)

    def plasma_view(self):
        """Return a grid view containing only plasma intervals."""

        return type(self)(s_nodes=self.s_nodes[: self.ni + 1], ni=self.ni, ivac=0)

    @classmethod
    def uniform(cls, surfs=101, ivac=0, dsvac=0.0):
        """Create a uniform plasma mesh plus optional uniform vacuum mesh."""

        if surfs < 2:
            raise ValueError("surfs must be at least 2.")
        ni = surfs - 1
        plasma = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, surfs)
        if ivac:
            vacuum = np.linspace(1.0, 1.0 + dsvac, ivac + 1)[1:]
            s_nodes = np.concatenate((plasma, vacuum))
        else:
            s_nodes = plasma
        return cls(s_nodes=s_nodes, ni=ni, ivac=ivac)

"""Native pseudo-vacuum geometry helpers for TERPSICHORE migration."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TerpsichoreVacmetData:
    """Metric arrays produced by the TERPSICHORE ``VACMET`` mapping."""

    bjac: np.ndarray
    gppl: np.ndarray
    gtpl: np.ndarray
    gttl: np.ndarray
    gssu: np.ndarray
    gstl: np.ndarray
    gssl: np.ndarray
    rvac: np.ndarray
    vp: np.ndarray

    def as_vacuum_grid_data(self):
        """Return the dictionary consumed by native vacuum ``FOURIN`` helpers."""

        return {
            "bjac": self.bjac,
            "gppl": self.gppl,
            "gtpl": self.gtpl,
            "gttl": self.gttl,
            "gssu": self.gssu,
            "gstl": self.gstl,
            "gssl": self.gssl,
        }


def _as_vector(values, name, size):
    arr = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    if arr.shape != (size,):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape ({size},), got {arr.shape}.")
    return arr


def _as_nodes(values, name, min_size):
    arr = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    if arr.ndim != 1 or arr.size < min_size:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be one-dimensional with at least {min_size} values.")
    return arr


def compute_vacmet_metrics(
    *,
    s_nodes,
    ni,
    ivac,
    dsvac,
    pvac,
    qvac,
    nowall,
    rpvi,
    vpvi,
    zpvi,
    rtpvi,
    vtpvi,
    ztpvi,
    rppvi,
    vppvi,
    zppvi,
    rspvi,
    vspvi,
    zspvi,
    rstpvi,
    vstpvi,
    zstpvi,
    rsppvi,
    vsppvi,
    zsppvi,
    rwall,
    zwall,
    rtwall,
    ztwall,
    rpwall,
    zpwall,
    tor=None,
):
    """Port TERPSICHORE ``VACMET`` pseudo-vacuum metric formulas.

    The returned arrays are restricted to pseudo-vacuum intervals and have shape
    ``(njk, ivac)``.  Interval ``0`` corresponds to Fortran radial index
    ``ni + 1``.  All geometry inputs are pointwise arrays on the angular
    ``jk`` grid.  This function intentionally mirrors the Fortran formulas in
    ``tprgl3_block_ap.f:VACMET`` and does not infer wall/boundary data.
    """

    if ivac < 0:
        raise ValueError("ivac must be non-negative.")
    s_nodes = _as_nodes(s_nodes, "s_nodes", ni + ivac + 1)
    if ivac == 0:
        empty = np.zeros((0, 0))
        return TerpsichoreVacmetData(
            bjac=empty,
            gppl=empty,
            gtpl=empty,
            gttl=empty,
            gssu=empty,
            gstl=empty,
            gssl=empty,
            rvac=empty,
            vp=np.zeros(0),
        )
    if dsvac == 0:
        raise ValueError("dsvac must be non-zero when ivac > 0.")

    base = np.asarray(rpvi, dtype=float)
    if base.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("VACMET geometry arrays must be one-dimensional.")
    njk = base.size
    names = {
        "rpvi": rpvi,
        "vpvi": vpvi,
        "zpvi": zpvi,
        "rtpvi": rtpvi,
        "vtpvi": vtpvi,
        "ztpvi": ztpvi,
        "rppvi": rppvi,
        "vppvi": vppvi,
        "zppvi": zppvi,
        "rspvi": rspvi,
        "vspvi": vspvi,
        "zspvi": zspvi,
        "rstpvi": rstpvi,
        "vstpvi": vstpvi,
        "zstpvi": zstpvi,
        "rsppvi": rsppvi,
        "vsppvi": vsppvi,
        "zsppvi": zsppvi,
        "rwall": rwall,
        "zwall": zwall,
        "rtwall": rtwall,
        "ztwall": ztwall,
        "rpwall": rpwall,
        "zpwall": zpwall,
    }
    arrays = {name: _as_vector(value, name, njk) for name, value in names.items()}
    if tor is None:
        tor_arr = np.zeros(njk)
    else:
        tor_arr = _as_vector(tor, "tor", njk)

    bjac = np.zeros((njk, ivac))
    gppl = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    gtpl = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    gttl = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    gssu = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    gstl = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    gssl = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    rvac = np.zeros_like(bjac)
    vp = np.zeros(ivac)
    nwalt = abs(nowall)
    wall_phase = tor_arr if nowall >= 0 else arrays["vpvi"]
    vpwall = np.ones(njk) if nowall >= 0 else arrays["vppvi"]
    vtwall = np.zeros(njk) if nowall >= 0 else arrays["vtpvi"]

    for interval in range(ivac):
        svach = 0.5 * (s_nodes[ni + interval + 1] + s_nodes[ni + interval])
        svac0 = svach - 1.0
        ratio = svac0 / dsvac
        svac1 = 1.0 - nwalt * ratio**pvac
        svac2 = svac0 * (1.0 - nwalt * ratio ** (pvac - 1.0))
        svac3 = nwalt * ratio**qvac
        svac4 = -nwalt * pvac / dsvac * ratio ** (pvac - 1.0)
        svac5 = 1.0 - nwalt * pvac * ratio ** (pvac - 1.0)
        svac6 = nwalt * qvac / dsvac * ratio ** (qvac - 1.0)

        rvac_i = svac1 * arrays["rpvi"] + svac3 * arrays["rwall"] + svac2 * arrays["rspvi"]
        rsvac = svac4 * arrays["rpvi"] + svac6 * arrays["rwall"] + svac5 * arrays["rspvi"]
        vsvac = svac4 * arrays["vpvi"] + svac6 * wall_phase + svac5 * arrays["vspvi"]
        zsvac = svac4 * arrays["zpvi"] + svac6 * arrays["zwall"] + svac5 * arrays["zspvi"]
        rtvac = svac1 * arrays["rtpvi"] + svac3 * arrays["rtwall"] + svac2 * arrays["rstpvi"]
        vtvac = svac1 * arrays["vtpvi"] + svac3 * vtwall + svac2 * arrays["vstpvi"]
        ztvac = svac1 * arrays["ztpvi"] + svac3 * arrays["ztwall"] + svac2 * arrays["zstpvi"]
        rpvac = svac1 * arrays["rppvi"] + svac3 * arrays["rpwall"] + svac2 * arrays["rsppvi"]
        vpvac = svac1 * arrays["vppvi"] + svac3 * vpwall + svac2 * arrays["vsppvi"]
        zpvac = svac1 * arrays["zppvi"] + svac3 * arrays["zpwall"] + svac2 * arrays["zsppvi"]

        bjac_i = rvac_i * (
            rsvac * (vtvac * zpvac - vpvac * ztvac)
            + vsvac * (ztvac * rpvac - zpvac * rtvac)
            + zsvac * (rtvac * vpvac - rpvac * vtvac)
        )
        if np.any(bjac_i == 0.0):
            raise ValueError("VACMET produced zero Jacobian values.")
        rvac[:, interval] = rvac_i
        bjac[:, interval] = bjac_i
        vp[interval] = -float(np.sum(bjac_i))

    Expected geometry keys are ``R``, ``Z``, ``phi`` or ``V`` plus first radial,
    poloidal, and toroidal derivatives using TERPSICHORE/DESC-like names:
    ``Rs/Rt/Rp``, ``Zs/Zt/Zp``, and ``phis/phit/phip`` or ``Vs/Vt/Vp``.
    Optional mixed radial derivatives ``Rst/Rsp/Zst/Zsp/phist/phisp`` are used
    when present; otherwise they default to zero.  Arrays may be either 1-D
    boundary arrays or 2-D ``(points, radial)`` arrays.

    def get(*names, default=None):
        for name in names:
            if name in geometry and geometry[name] is not None:

            return default

        arr = np.asarray(value, dtype=float)

            return arr

    zeros = np.zeros_like(rpvi)

        "vpvi": boundary(get("phi", "V"), "phi"),
        "zpvi": boundary(get("Z"), "Z"),
        "rtpvi": boundary(get("Rt", "R_theta"), "Rt"),
        "vtpvi": boundary(get("phit", "Vt", "phi_theta"), "phit"),
        "ztpvi": boundary(get("Zt", "Z_theta"), "Zt"),
        "rppvi": boundary(get("Rp", "R_zeta"), "Rp"),
        "vppvi": boundary(get("phip", "Vp", "phi_zeta"), "phip"),
        "zppvi": boundary(get("Zp", "Z_zeta"), "Zp"),
        "rspvi": boundary(get("Rs", "R_s"), "Rs"),
        "vspvi": boundary(get("phis", "Vs", "phi_s"), "phis"),
        "zspvi": boundary(get("Zs", "Z_s"), "Zs"),
        "rstpvi": boundary(get("Rst", "R_st", "R_s_theta", default=zeros), "Rst"),
        "vstpvi": boundary(get("phist", "Vst", "phi_st", "phi_s_theta", default=zeros), "phist"),
        "zstpvi": boundary(get("Zst", "Z_st", "Z_s_theta", default=zeros), "Zst"),
        "rsppvi": boundary(get("Rsp", "R_sp", "R_s_zeta", default=zeros), "Rsp"),
        "vsppvi": boundary(get("phisp", "Vsp", "phi_sp", "phi_s_zeta", default=zeros), "phisp"),
        "zsppvi": boundary(get("Zsp", "Z_sp", "Z_s_zeta", default=zeros), "Zsp"),
    }
    for name, value in out.items():
        if value.shape != rpvi.shape:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {rpvi.shape}, got {value.shape}.")

def build_vacmet_inputs(
    *,
    s_nodes,
    ni,
    ivac,
    dsvac,
    pvac,
    qvac,
    nowall,
    boundary,
    wall=None,
    wall_scale=1.0,
    tor=None,
):
    """Build ``compute_vacmet_metrics`` inputs from native boundary/wall arrays.

    ``boundary`` must provide the plasma-boundary arrays named in
    ``_VACMET_GEOMETRY_NAMES``.  ``wall`` may provide ``rwall/zwall`` and their
    derivatives.  When ``wall`` is omitted, a simple scaled-boundary wall is
    generated by multiplying R-like arrays by ``wall_scale`` and copying Z-like
    arrays, matching the shape and derivative contract expected by VACMET.
    """

    if wall_scale <= 0:
        raise ValueError("wall_scale must be positive.")
    boundary_arrays = {name: np.asarray(boundary[name], dtype=float) for name in _VACMET_GEOMETRY_NAMES}
    njk = boundary_arrays["rpvi"].shape
    if len(njk) != 1:
        raise ValueError("VACMET boundary arrays must be one-dimensional.")
    for name, value in boundary_arrays.items():
        if value.shape != njk:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {njk}, got {value.shape}.")
    if tor is None:
        tor_arr = np.zeros(njk[0])
    else:
        tor_arr = _as_vector(tor, "tor", njk[0])
    if wall is None:
        wall_arrays = {
            "rwall": wall_scale * boundary_arrays["rpvi"],
            "zwall": boundary_arrays["zpvi"].copy(),
            "rtwall": wall_scale * boundary_arrays["rtpvi"],
            "ztwall": boundary_arrays["ztpvi"].copy(),
            "rpwall": wall_scale * boundary_arrays["rppvi"],
            "zpwall": boundary_arrays["zppvi"].copy(),
        }
    else:
        wall_arrays = {
            name: _as_vector(wall[name], name, njk[0])
            for name in ("rwall", "zwall", "rtwall", "ztwall", "rpwall", "zpwall")
        }
    return {
        "s_nodes": np.asarray(s_nodes, dtype=float),
        "ni": int(ni),
        "ivac": int(ivac),
        "dsvac": float(dsvac),
        "pvac": float(pvac),
        "qvac": float(qvac),
        "nowall": int(nowall),
        **boundary_arrays,
        **wall_arrays,
        "tor": tor_arr,
    }



def vacuum_grid_data_from_vacmet_inputs(vacmet_inputs):
    """Return native vacuum ``FOURIN`` grid data from VACMET input arrays.

    This is the native entry point for the VACMET stage: callers may
    provide boundary, wall, and pseudo-vacuum controls from DESC/native geometry
    instead of loading a converted Fortran dump.
    """

    return compute_vacmet_metrics(**vacmet_inputs).as_vacuum_grid_data()

"""Fourier mode tables for TERPSICHORE stability perturbations."""

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TerpsichoreModeTable:
    """Stability perturbation Fourier mode table.

    The table stores TERPSICHORE-style poloidal/toroidal mode pairs ``(m, n)``
    and axis regularity exponents.  It intentionally keeps a compact data model
    so the Fortran ``STABIN`` mode filtering rules can be ported incrementally.
    """

    m: np.ndarray
    n: np.ndarray
    mode_family: int = -1
    nfp: int = 1
    parity: str = "cos"
    frozen: np.ndarray | None = None
    ql: np.ndarray | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        m = np.asarray(self.m, dtype=int)
        n = np.asarray(self.n, dtype=int)
        if m.ndim != 1 or n.ndim != 1 or m.shape != n.shape:
            raise ValueError("m and n must be one-dimensional arrays with equal length.")
        if np.any(m < 0):
            raise ValueError("TERPSICHORE poloidal mode numbers must be non-negative.")
        if self.nfp <= 0:
            raise ValueError("nfp must be positive.")
        if self.parity not in {"cos", "sin"}:
            raise ValueError("parity must be 'cos' or 'sin'.")
        frozen = np.zeros(m.shape, dtype=bool) if self.frozen is None else self.frozen
        frozen = np.asarray(frozen, dtype=bool)
        if frozen.shape != m.shape:
            raise ValueError("frozen must have the same shape as m and n.")
        ql = self.axis_regularization(m) if self.ql is None else self.ql
        ql = np.asarray(ql, dtype=float)
        if ql.shape != m.shape:
            raise ValueError("ql must have the same shape as m and n.")
        object.__setattr__(self, "m", m)
        object.__setattr__(self, "n", n)
        object.__setattr__(self, "frozen", frozen)
        object.__setattr__(self, "ql", ql)

    @property
    def size(self):
        """Number of retained stability modes."""

        return self.m.size

    @property
    def modes(self):
        """Return an ``(size, 2)`` array of ``(m, n)`` mode pairs."""

        return np.column_stack((self.m, self.n))

    @staticmethod
    def axis_regularization(m):
        """Return TERPSICHORE-compatible axis exponents for ``XI``.

        The full Fortran implementation contains additional parity-dependent
        details.  This migration-safe default captures the documented behavior:
        non-``m=1`` modes vanish on axis, while ``m=1`` uses the special scaled
        regularity branch.
        """

        m = np.asarray(m, dtype=int)
        return np.where(m == 1, 0.5, np.maximum(m, 1)).astype(float)

    @classmethod
    def from_bounds(
        cls,
        *,
        M_max=8,
        N_min=-4,
        N_max=4,
        mode_family=-1,
        nfp=1,
        parity="cos",
    ):
        """Build a mode table from DESC-native bounds.

        For ``mode_family < 0`` this includes every ``n`` in ``[N_min, N_max]``.
        Otherwise it retains toroidal modes satisfying the TERPSICHORE family
        relation ``n = i * nfp ± mode_family``.
        """

        if M_max < 0:
            raise ValueError("M_max must be non-negative.")
        if N_min > N_max:
            raise ValueError("N_min must be <= N_max.")
        if nfp <= 0:
            raise ValueError("nfp must be positive.")
        modes = []
        for n in range(N_min, N_max + 1):
            if mode_family >= 0:
                remainder = abs(n) % nfp
                family = min(remainder, nfp - remainder)
                if family != mode_family:
                    continue
            for m in range(M_max + 1):
                modes.append((m, n))
        if not modes:
            raise ValueError("mode bounds produced an empty TERPSICHORE mode table.")
        arr = np.asarray(modes, dtype=int)
        return cls(
            arr[:, 0],
            arr[:, 1],
            mode_family=mode_family,
            nfp=nfp,
            parity=parity,
        )

def boozer_poloidal_flip_permutation(mode_m, mode_n):
    """Return the mode permutation and sign of a Boozer poloidal-angle flip.

    TERPSICHORE inherits VMEC's left-handed ``(s, theta, zeta)`` frame, in which
    the coordinate Jacobian is negative.  DESC stores every equilibrium in a
    right-handed frame: :func:`desc.compat.ensure_positive_jacobian` converts a
    left-handed input by "switching the sign of theta" (it negates all ``m < 0``
    Fourier coefficients of ``R``/``Z`` together with ``iota``), and
    ``desc.external.terpsichore._write_wout`` performs the inverse operation when
    it writes a ``wout`` file for the Fortran code.  Therefore

    ``theta_TERPSICHORE = -theta_DESC``,  ``zeta_TERPSICHORE = zeta_DESC``.

    A field expanded as ``sum_mn f_mn cos(m*theta - n*zeta)`` in the DESC frame
    becomes ``sum_mn f_{m,-n} cos(m*theta' - n*zeta)`` in the flipped frame, while
    a sine-parity field additionally changes sign for every ``m >= 1``.  Modes
    with ``m = 0`` are invariant.  This helper returns the index permutation
    ``(m, n) -> (m, -n)`` and the sine-parity sign factor, and it fails loudly if
    the mode table is not closed under ``n -> -n`` for ``m >= 1``, because in that
    case the frame change cannot be represented without discarding content.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mode_m, mode_n : array-like of int
        Boozer mode table (absolute toroidal mode numbers).

    Returns
    -------
    permutation : ndarray of int
        Index array with ``permutation[i]`` the position of ``(m_i, -n_i)``.
    sign : ndarray of float
        ``-1`` for ``m >= 1`` and ``+1`` for ``m = 0``; applies to sine-parity
        spectra only.

    """

    mode_m = _integer_mode_array(mode_m, "mode_m")
    mode_n = _integer_mode_array(mode_n, "mode_n")
    if mode_m.shape != mode_n.shape:
        raise ValueError("mode_m and mode_n must have identical shapes.")
    lookup = {}
    for index, mode in enumerate(zip(mode_m, mode_n)):
        mode = (int(mode[0]), int(mode[1]))
        if mode in lookup:
            raise ValueError(f"Boozer mode table contains duplicate mode {mode}.")
        lookup[mode] = index
    permutation = np.arange(mode_m.size, dtype=int)
    sign = np.ones(mode_m.size, dtype=float)
    for index, (m, n) in enumerate(zip(mode_m, mode_n)):
        m = int(m)
        n = int(n)
        if m == 0:
            continue
        mirrored = lookup.get((m, -n))
        if mirrored is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "The Boozer mode table must be closed under n -> -n for m >= 1 to "
                f"represent the TERPSICHORE poloidal orientation; mode {(m, -n)} "
                "is missing."
            )
        permutation[index] = mirrored
        sign[index] = -1.0

def flip_boozer_poloidal_orientation(*, mode_m, mode_n, spectra):
    """Convert DESC-frame Boozer spectra to TERPSICHORE's poloidal orientation.

    See :func:`boozer_poloidal_flip_permutation` for the convention.  Cosine
    parity amplitudes (``fr``, ``fbsq``, ``fbjac``, ``fsigmb``, ``ftaub``,

        raise TypeError("spectra must be a TerpsichoreVmtoboSpectra instance.")

def terpsichore_edge_extrapolation(values):
    """Extrapolate a half-surface profile to the boundary as TERPSICHORE does.

    Fortran ``EXTINT``/``VACMET`` obtain boundary values from the outermost two
    half surfaces with ``1.5*f(ni) - 0.5*f(ni-1)``.
    """

    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if values.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("cannot extrapolate an empty profile.")
    if values.size == 1:
        return float(values[-1])
    return float(1.5 * values[-1] - 0.5 * values[-2])


def _coordinate_volume_jacobian(metric_inputs):
    """Return the cylindrical volume Jacobian of a Boozer coordinate mapping."""

    R = metric_inputs["R"]
    return R * (
        metric_inputs["Rs"]
        * (metric_inputs["phvt"] * metric_inputs["Zp"] - metric_inputs["phvp"] * metric_inputs["Zt"])
        + metric_inputs["phvs"]
        * (metric_inputs["Zt"] * metric_inputs["Rp"] - metric_inputs["Zp"] * metric_inputs["Rt"])
        + metric_inputs["Zs"]
        * (metric_inputs["Rt"] * metric_inputs["phvp"] - metric_inputs["Rp"] * metric_inputs["phvt"])
    )


def _project_desc_boozer_quadrature(
    eq, *, rho, nper, njq, nkq, mode_m, mode_n
):
    """Project DESC geometry onto Boozer spectra with one angular quadrature grid.

    The quadrature grid is deliberately decoupled from the TERPSICHORE angular
    reconstruction grid: the DESC integrands ``R``, ``Z``, ``|B|^2`` and the
    angular map determinant are nonlinear in the equilibrium spectra, so the
    Boozer projection integrals need more quadrature nodes than the number of
    retained Boozer harmonics to avoid aliasing.
    """

    from desc.grid import LinearGrid

    theta = np.arange(njq, dtype=float) * (2.0 * np.pi / njq)
    zeta = np.arange(nkq, dtype=float) * (2.0 * np.pi / (nkq * nper))
    source_grid = LinearGrid(
        rho=rho, theta=theta, zeta=zeta, NFP=nper, sym=False, endpoint=False
    )
    computed = eq.compute(list(_DESC_BOOZER_COMPUTE_NAMES), grid=source_grid)
    fields = {
        name: _desc_half_grid_field(computed[name], source_grid, rho)
        for name in _DESC_BOOZER_COMPUTE_NAMES
    }
    mapping = compute_desc_boozer_angular_mapping(
        theta_b=fields["theta_B"],
        zeta_b=fields["zeta_B"],
        theta_b_t=fields["theta_PEST_t"] + fields["iota"] * fields["nu_t"],
        theta_b_z=fields["theta_PEST_z"] + fields["iota"] * fields["nu_z"],
        zeta_b_t=fields["phi_t"] + fields["nu_t"],
        zeta_b_z=fields["phi_z"] + fields["nu_z"],
        jacobian=fields["sqrt(g)_Boozer_DESC"],
    )
    # TERPSICHORE's BJAC is sqrt(g) with respect to (s, theta, zeta); DESC
    # returns sqrt(g) with respect to (rho, theta, zeta) and uses the opposite
    # poloidal orientation, hence the factor -1/(2*rho) with s = rho**2.
    spectra = project_desc_geometry_to_boozer_spectra(
        mapping=mapping,
        mode_m=mode_m,
        mode_n=mode_n,
        R=fields["R"],
        Z=fields["Z"],
        phi_t=fields["phi_t"],
        phi_z=fields["phi_z"],
        bsq=fields["|B|^2"],
        bjac_source=-fields["sqrt(g)"] / (2.0 * np.asarray(rho, dtype=float)[None, :]),
        dtdp=1.0 / (njq * nkq),
    )
    return fields, mapping, spectra, source_grid

    equilibrium_data,
    *,
    M_booz_max=None,
    N_booz_max=None,
    nj=40,
    nk=40,
    radial_grid=None,
    quadrature_factor=None,
    quadrature_factors=(2, 4, 8),
    reconstruction_tolerance=1e-9,
    reconstruction_limit=1e-2,
    max_quadrature_nodes=1 << 21,
):
    """Map an arbitrary stellarator-symmetric DESC equilibrium to Boozer geometry.

    The equilibrium is sampled on TERPSICHORE half surfaces (``s = rho**2``) in
    DESC coordinates.  Physical ``R``, ``Z``, ``phi``, ``|B|^2`` and the coordinate
    Jacobian are projected with the exact angular coordinate determinant onto
    TERPSICHORE's Boozer Fourier basis, the poloidal orientation is converted to
    TERPSICHORE's left-handed frame (see
    :func:`flip_boozer_poloidal_orientation`), ``EXTINT`` supplies integer
    surfaces and ``METRIC`` uses the original radial staggering.

    Two angular grids appear here and must not be confused:

    * the *reconstruction* grid ``(nj, nk)`` on which every TERPSICHORE real-space
      geometry array and every subsequent ``FOURIN`` integral is evaluated.  It is
      raised to the Nyquist limit ``2*M_booz + 1`` / ``2*N_booz + 1`` of the
      retained Boozer harmonics when the caller asks for less;
    * the *quadrature* grid used for the Boozer projection integrals, which is a
      multiple of the reconstruction grid.  The multiple is increased until the
      reconstructed angular Jacobian factor ``SIGMAB`` reproduces its exact value
      to ``reconstruction_tolerance``.  For an isotropic equilibrium
      ``SIGMAB == 1`` identically, so ``max|SIGMAB - 1|`` is an exact, equilibrium
      independent measure of the combined aliasing and truncation error of the
      transform.

    Returns
    -------
    TerpsichoreDescBoozerData
        Boozer mode table, trigonometric tables, spectra, integer-surface data,
        ``METRIC`` inputs, radial profiles, boundary data for ``VACMET`` and
        transform diagnostics.

    """

    eq = getattr(equilibrium_data, "equilibrium", None)
    if eq is None:
        raise TerpsichoreMigrationNotImplementedError(
            "Direct DESC Boozer mapping requires the originating Equilibrium object."
        )
    if not bool(getattr(equilibrium_data, "sym", getattr(eq, "sym", False))):
        raise TerpsichoreMigrationNotImplementedError(
            "TERPSICHORE's equilibrium Fourier representation requires "
            "stellarator symmetry."
        )
    radial_grid = equilibrium_data.radial_grid if radial_grid is None else radial_grid
    nper = int(getattr(eq, "NFP", equilibrium_data.nfp))
    if nper <= 0:
        raise ValueError("The number of field periods must be positive.")
    M_desc = int(getattr(eq, "M", 0))
    N_desc = int(getattr(eq, "N", 0))
    M_booz_max = 2 * M_desc if M_booz_max is None else int(M_booz_max)
    N_booz_max = 2 * N_desc if N_booz_max is None else int(N_booz_max)

        raise ValueError("Boozer mode bounds must be non-negative.")

        # n != 0 harmonics would only add quadrature noise.

    nj_grid = max(int(nj), 2 * M_booz_max + 1)
    nk_grid = max(int(nk), 2 * N_booz_max + 1)

            eq, rho=rho, nper=nper, njq=njq, nkq=nkq, mode_m=mode_m, mode_n=mode_n
        )

            "The DESC-to-Boozer transform did not converge: the reconstructed "
            f"angular Jacobian factor deviates from unity by {best['residual']:.3e} "
            f"with a {best['nj']}x{best['nk']} quadrature grid and Boozer bounds "

            "N_booz_max, or supply a better converged equilibrium."

        mode_m=mode_m,
        mode_n=mode_n,
        fr=spectra.fr,
        fz=spectra.fz,
        fphv=spectra.fphv,

        mode_m=mode_m,
        mode_n=mode_n,

        base_phv=trig["tor"],

        "cj": cj,
        "civ": ci,
        "cjv": cj,
        "cip": np.gradient(ci, s_centers, edge_order=edge_order),
        "cjp": np.gradient(cj, s_centers, edge_order=edge_order),

        "rho_nodes": rho,
        "s_centers": s_centers,
        "nj": nj_grid,
        "nk": nk_grid,
        "nper": nper,
        "dtdp": dtdp,

        "fpp_edge": terpsichore_edge_extrapolation(fpp),

def boozer_boundary_from_integer_spectra(
    *, mode_m, mode_n, tcos, tsin, tor, integer_grid, s_nodes
):
    """Build ``VACMET`` plasma-boundary arrays from integer-surface Boozer spectra.

    ``VACMET`` blends the plasma boundary, its radial derivative and a wall shape
    across the pseudo-vacuum intervals, so it needs ``R``, ``Z`` and the toroidal
    angle map ``V`` at ``s = 1`` together with their first angular derivatives,
    their radial derivatives, and the mixed radial/angular derivatives.  Every
    array is evaluated on the same angular grid as the plasma geometry, which
    keeps the boundary data meaning unchanged when plasma and vacuum intervals
    are concatenated.
    """

    mode_m = _integer_mode_array(mode_m, "mode_m")
    mode_n = _integer_mode_array(mode_n, "mode_n")
    tcos = np.asarray(tcos, dtype=float)
    tsin = np.asarray(tsin, dtype=float)
    tor = np.asarray(tor, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    s_nodes = np.asarray(s_nodes, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    fri = np.asarray(integer_grid.fri, dtype=float)
    fzi = np.asarray(integer_grid.fzi, dtype=float)
    fphvi = np.asarray(integer_grid.fphvi, dtype=float)
    if fri.shape[1] != s_nodes.size:
        raise ValueError(
            "integer-surface spectra and s_nodes must share the radial axis."
        )
    if s_nodes.size < 2:
        raise ValueError("boundary radial derivatives need at least two surfaces.")
    edge_order = 2 if s_nodes.size > 2 else 1
    m = mode_m[:, None]
    n = mode_n[:, None]

    def radial(spectrum):
        return np.gradient(spectrum, s_nodes, axis=1, edge_order=edge_order)[:, -1]

    fr = fri[:, -1]
    fz = fzi[:, -1]
    fv = fphvi[:, -1]
    frs = radial(fri)
    fzs = radial(fzi)
    fvs = radial(fphvi)
    m1 = mode_m
    n1 = mode_n
    return {
        "rpvi": tcos @ fr,
        "zpvi": tsin @ fz,
        "vpvi": tor + tsin @ fv,
        "rtpvi": tsin @ (-m1 * fr),
        "ztpvi": tcos @ (m1 * fz),
        "vtpvi": tcos @ (m1 * fv),
        "rppvi": tsin @ (n1 * fr),
        "zppvi": tcos @ (-n1 * fz),
        "vppvi": 1.0 + tcos @ (-n1 * fv),
        "rspvi": tcos @ frs,
        "zspvi": tsin @ fzs,
        "vspvi": tsin @ fvs,
        "rstpvi": tsin @ (-m1 * frs),
        "zstpvi": tcos @ (m1 * fzs),
        "vstpvi": tcos @ (m1 * fvs),
        "rsppvi": tsin @ (n1 * frs),
        "zsppvi": tcos @ (-n1 * fzs),
        "vsppvi": tcos @ (-n1 * fvs),
        "boundary_spectra": {
            "fr": fr,
            "fz": fz,
            "fv": fv,
            "frs": frs,
            "fzs": fzs,
            "fvs": fvs,
            "mode_m": mode_m,
            "mode_n": mode_n,
        },
    }

    equilibrium_data, *, radial_grid=None, cache=True, **transform_options
):
    """Return the native DESC-to-Boozer transform for an equilibrium.

    The transform is expensive (it evaluates DESC geometry on a refined angular
    quadrature grid), so the result is cached in
    ``equilibrium_data.data["terpsichore_boozer"]`` and reused by the geometry,
    coefficient and vacuum stages.  Caching is keyed on the requested transform
    options so a resolution change recomputes the transform.
    """

    data = equilibrium_data.data
    radial_grid = equilibrium_data.radial_grid if radial_grid is None else radial_grid
    key = (
        int(radial_grid.ni),
        tuple(sorted((name, _hashable_option(value)) for name, value in transform_options.items())),
    )
    if cache:
        cached = data.get("terpsichore_boozer")
        if isinstance(cached, TerpsichoreDescBoozerData) and data.get(
            "terpsichore_boozer_key"
        ) == key:
            return cached
    transform = transform_desc_geometry_to_boozer(
        equilibrium_data, radial_grid=radial_grid, **transform_options
    )
    if cache:
        data["terpsichore_boozer"] = transform
        data["terpsichore_boozer_key"] = key
    return transform

def fourin_inputs_from_geometry(
    equilibrium_data,
    geometry=None,
    strict=False,
    modelk=0,
    *,
    boozer=None,
    radial_grid=None,
    transform_options=None,
):
    """Build FOURIN ``grid_data`` and profiles from DESC/native data.

    In default mode this preserves the migration smoke-test adapter: native
    TERPSICHORE fields are preferred and limited DESC fallbacks are recorded in
    diagnostics.  In ``strict=True`` mode the function refuses approximations and
    computes METRIC/BOPHYS fields from explicit TERPSICHORE Boozer arrays using
    ``compute_strict_boozer_metric``.

    ``radial_grid`` selects the intervals that the returned arrays cover.  For a
    full-domain run (``ivac > 0``) the caller passes ``radial_grid.plasma_view()``
    so that plasma arrays keep their meaning and the pseudo-vacuum intervals are
    supplied separately by ``VACMET``.
    """

    geometry = compute_desc_geometry(equilibrium_data) if geometry is None else geometry
    data = dict(equilibrium_data.data)
    radial_grid = equilibrium_data.radial_grid if radial_grid is None else radial_grid
    diagnostics = {"approximated_fields": [], "strict": bool(strict), "modelk": modelk}
    require_ko_fields = bool(strict and modelk in {1, 3})
    if strict:
        data.update(
            strict_geometry_mapping_from_desc(
                equilibrium_data,
                geometry,
                boozer=boozer,
                radial_grid=radial_grid,
                transform_options=transform_options,
            )
        )
        transform = data.get("desc_boozer_transform")
        if transform is not None:
            diagnostics["boozer_transform"] = dict(transform.diagnostics)

473	def compute_fourin_vacuum_integral_arrays_from_grid(*, vacuum_grid_data, trig_table):
474	    """Compute vacuum-domain raw ``cna``/``cnb`` arrays for TERPSICHORE ``FOURIN``.
475	
476	    The vacuum branch requires ``gppl``, ``gtpl``, ``gttl``, ``gstl``, ``gssl``
477	    and ``gssu`` on pseudo-vacuum intervals ``ni+1..nvi``. Callers must provide
478	    the complete metric terms from strict vacuum geometry reconstruction.
479	    """
480	
481	    required = ("gppl", "gtpl", "gttl", "gstl", "gssl", "gssu")
482	    missing = [name for name in required if vacuum_grid_data.get(name) is None]
483	    if missing:
484	        raise ValueError(
485	            "vacuum FOURIN requires metric arrays "
486	            + ", ".join(required)
487	            + f"; missing {tuple(missing)}"
488	        )
489	    arrays = {name: np.asarray(vacuum_grid_data[name], dtype=float) for name in required}
490	    shapes = {name: value.shape for name, value in arrays.items()}
491	    if len(set(shapes.values())) != 1:
492	        raise ValueError(f"vacuum metric arrays must have identical shapes, got {shapes}")
493	    points, intervals = next(iter(shapes.values()))
494	    if trig_table.tsc.shape[1] != points or trig_table.tss.shape[1] != points:
495	        raise ValueError("vacuum metric point count must match trigonometric tables.")
496	    lss_with_sentinel = trig_table.lss + 1
497	    cna = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel, intervals))
498	    cnb = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel, intervals))
499	    cna[1] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gppl"]
500	    cna[2] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gtpl"]
501	    cna[3] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gttl"]
502	    cnb[1] = trig_table.tss @ arrays["gstl"]
503	    cnb[2] = trig_table.tsc @ arrays["gssl"]
504	    cnb[3] = trig_table.tss @ arrays["gssu"]
505	    return cna, cnb

def generate_coefficients_from_geometry(
    equilibrium_data,
    mode_table,
    radial_grid=None,
    *,
    geometry=None,
    boozer=None,
    trig_table=None,
    modelk=0,
    strict=True,
    transform_options=None,
    fixed_boundary=True,
    igreen=0,
    cospar=1.0,
    cospr2=1.0,
    dtdp=None,
):
    """Generate TERPSICHORE ``c0..c11`` from equilibrium geometry (native ``FOURIN``).

    This is the native replacement for Fortran ``FOURIN``.  The Boozer geometry
    stage (``VMTOBO``/``EXTINT``/``METRIC``/``BOPHYS``) supplies the real-space
    metric, current and curvature arrays on the plasma intervals selected by
    ``radial_grid``; the stability mode table supplies the perturbation harmonics.
    Both are evaluated on *one* angular grid so that the Fourier integrals

    ``cna/cnb[i, lsx(m_c -+ m_r, n_c -+ n_r)] = sum_jk trig * f_i * |BJAC|``

    use the same mode ordering and the same radial (half-surface) convention as
    the geometry stage.

    Parameters
    ----------
    equilibrium_data : TerpsichoreEquilibriumData
        Equilibrium container; the native DESC-to-Boozer transform is taken from
        it (and cached there) when ``boozer`` is not supplied.
    mode_table : TerpsichoreModeTable
        Stability perturbation harmonics.
    radial_grid : TerpsichoreRadialGrid, optional
        Radial mesh whose intervals the coefficients cover.  For a full-domain run
        the caller passes the plasma view; the pseudo-vacuum intervals come from
        :func:`map_fourin_vacuum_grid_to_coefficients`.
    trig_table : TerpsichoreTrigTable, optional
        Pre-built stability trigonometric table.  When omitted it is built on the
        geometry stage's own ``(POL, TOR)`` grid, which is required for the
        integrals above to be consistent.
    dtdp : float, optional
        Angular quadrature weight ``1/(nj*nk)``.  Defaults to the geometry grid's
        own weight.

    Returns
    -------
    coefficients : TerpsichoreCoefficientData
    trig_table : TerpsichoreTrigTable
    diagnostics : dict

    """

    from .geometry import (
        boozer_transform_for_equilibrium_data,
        fourin_inputs_from_geometry,
    )
    from .trig import build_trig_table

    if radial_grid is None:
        radial_grid = equilibrium_data.radial_grid
    if boozer is None and strict and getattr(equilibrium_data, "equilibrium", None) is not None:
        boozer = boozer_transform_for_equilibrium_data(
            equilibrium_data,
            radial_grid=radial_grid,
            **(transform_options or {}),
        )
    grid_data, profiles, diagnostics = fourin_inputs_from_geometry(
        equilibrium_data,
        geometry,
        strict=strict,
        modelk=modelk,
        boozer=boozer,
        radial_grid=radial_grid,
        transform_options=transform_options,
    )
    nper = int(getattr(equilibrium_data, "nfp", 1))
    pol = tor = None
    nj = nk = None
    if boozer is not None:
        pol = boozer.pol
        tor = boozer.tor
        nper = int(boozer.profiles.get("nper", nper))
        nj = int(boozer.profiles["nj"])
        nk = int(boozer.profiles["nk"])
        if dtdp is None:
            dtdp = float(boozer.profiles["dtdp"])
    if trig_table is None:
        if pol is None:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "Native FOURIN needs the geometry stage's angular grid; supply "
                "a trig_table or a native Boozer transform."
            )
        trig_table = build_trig_table(
            mode_table, nj=nj, nk=nk, nper=nper, pol=pol, tor=tor
        )
    points = np.asarray(grid_data["bjac"], dtype=float).shape[0]
    if trig_table.tsc.shape[1] != points:
        raise ValueError(
            "FOURIN angular grids disagree: the geometry arrays have "
            f"{points} points and the trigonometric table has "
            f"{trig_table.tsc.shape[1]}."
        )
    if dtdp is None:
        dtdp = 1.0 / points
    coefficients = map_fourin_grid_to_coefficients(
        grid_data=grid_data,
        profiles=profiles,
        mode_table=mode_table,
        trig_table=trig_table,
        modelk=modelk,
        dtdp=float(dtdp),
        cospar=float(cospar),
        cospr2=float(cospr2),
        fixed_boundary=bool(fixed_boundary),
        igreen=int(igreen),
    )
    diagnostics = dict(diagnostics)
    diagnostics.update(
        {
            "angular_points": int(points),
            "dtdp": float(dtdp),
            "cospar": float(cospar),
            "cospr2": float(cospr2),
            "intervals": int(np.asarray(profiles["ftp"]).size),
            "mode_count": int(mode_table.size),
            "fourin_modes": int(trig_table.lss),
            "fixed_boundary": bool(fixed_boundary),
            "igreen": int(igreen),
        }
    )
    return coefficients, trig_table, diagnostics

def assemble_potential_blocks(equilibrium_data, mode_table, radial_grid, options):
    """Assemble TERPSICHORE potential-energy blocks.

    This implements the coefficient-driven plasma branch of Fortran ``LHSMAT``.
    It expects precomputed TERPSICHORE coefficients and profiles in
    ``equilibrium_data.data["terpsichore_coefficients"]``. Coefficient generation
    from DESC geometry is a separate migration step.
    """

    coeffs = _get_coefficients(equilibrium_data)
    required = {
        "c0",
        "c1",
        "c2",
        "c4",
        "c5",
        "c6",
        "c9",
        "ftp",
        "fpp",
        "ftpp",
        "fppp",
        "ci",
        "cj",
    }
    if required.issubset(coeffs):
        return assemble_potential_blocks_from_coefficients(
            c0=coeffs["c0"],
            c1=coeffs["c1"],
            c2=coeffs["c2"],
            c4=coeffs["c4"],
            c5=coeffs["c5"],
            c6=coeffs["c6"],
            c9=coeffs["c9"],
            ftp=coeffs["ftp"],
            fpp=coeffs["fpp"],
            ftpp=coeffs["ftpp"],
            fppp=coeffs["fppp"],
            ci=coeffs["ci"],
            cj=coeffs["cj"],
            radial_grid=radial_grid,
            mode_table=mode_table,
            fixed_boundary=coeffs.get("fixed_boundary", options.vacuum.ivac == 0),
            igreen=coeffs.get("igreen", 0),
        )
    raise TerpsichoreMigrationNotImplementedError(
        "Potential-energy assembly needs TERPSICHORE coefficients c0,c1,c2,c4,c5,"
        "c6,c9 and profiles ftp,fpp,ftpp,fppp,ci,cj. Port coefficient generation "
        "or provide equilibrium_data.data['terpsichore_coefficients']."
    )


def _get_coefficients(equilibrium_data):
    raw = equilibrium_data.data.get("terpsichore_coefficients", {})
    if isinstance(raw, TerpsichoreCoefficientData):
        return raw.as_legacy_dict()
    return raw


def _profile_value(values, interval):
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    if values.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("TERPSICHORE profile arrays must be one-dimensional.")
    if values.size <= interval:
        raise ValueError("TERPSICHORE profile arrays are shorter than the radial grid.")
    return values[interval]


def _validate_coefficient_arrays(arrays, expected):
    for name, arr in arrays.items():
        if arr.shape != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {expected}, got {arr.shape}.")


def assemble_potential_blocks_from_coefficients(

def solve_blocks(potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid, mode_table, solver_options):
    """Solve TERPSICHORE block matrices with the selected solver."""

    if solver_options.solver == "pamera":
        return TerpsichoreBlockEigenSolver(
            al0=solver_options.al0,
            maxiter=solver_options.maxiter,
            tol=solver_options.tol,
        ).solve(potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid, mode_table)
    eigvals, eigvecs = solve_dense_blocks(
        potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid, mode_table
    )
    eigval = float(np.real(eigvals[0]))
    eigvec = np.real(eigvecs[:, 0])
    result = compute_energy_from_vector(
        eigvec,
        potential_blocks,
        kinetic_blocks,
        radial_grid,
        mode_table,
        diagnostics={"solver": "scipy", "dense_eigenvalue": eigval},
    )
    dominant_modes = compute_parvec(
        mode_table, result.eigenvector_xi, result.eigenvector_eta
    )
    return result.__class__(
        growth_rate=result.growth_rate,
        omega2=result.omega2,
        wp=result.wp,
        wk=result.wk,
        eigenvector_xi=result.eigenvector_xi,
        eigenvector_eta=result.eigenvector_eta,
        dominant_modes=dominant_modes,
        negative_eigenvalue_count=int(np.sum(np.real(eigvals) < 0)),
        mode_table=mode_table,
        radial_grid=radial_grid,
        diagnostics=result.diagnostics,
    )


def solve_dense_blocks(potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid, mode_table):
    """Assemble TERPSICHORE blocks and solve the dense generalized problem."""

    K, M = assemble_global_matrices(
        potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid, mode_table
    )
    return solve_dense_generalized(K, M)


def solve_dense_generalized(K, M):
    """Small dense fallback for tests once global matrices are available.

    TERPSICHORE matrices can include boundary/constrained variables with zero
    kinetic-energy rows.  For this dense migration helper we solve only on the
    active finite-mass subspace and expand eigenvectors back to full size.
    """

    K = np.asarray(K, dtype=float)
    M = np.asarray(M, dtype=float)
    active = (np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0) + np.linalg.norm(M, axis=1)) > 1e-14
    if not np.any(active):
        raise ValueError("mass matrix has no active finite-mass subspace")
    K_active = K[np.ix_(active, active)]
    M_active = M[np.ix_(active, active)]
    try:
        eigvals, eigvecs_active = np.linalg.eig(np.linalg.solve(M_active, K_active))
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError as err:
        raise ValueError("failed to solve dense generalized eigenproblem") from err
    if np.max(np.abs(eigvals.imag)) > 1e-8:
        raise TerpsichoreMigrationNotImplementedError(
            "dense generalized solve produced complex eigenvalues; sparse/Hermitian "
            "solver migration is needed for this case."
        )
    eigvecs = np.zeros((K.shape[0], eigvecs_active.shape[1]))
    eigvecs[active, :] = eigvecs_active.real
    order = np.argsort(eigvals.real)
    return eigvals[order].real, eigvecs[:, order].real


def pack_global_vector(xi, eta):
    """Pack ``XI`` and ``ETA`` arrays as ``[XI nodes, ETA intervals]``."""

    xi = np.asarray(xi, dtype=float)
    eta = np.asarray(eta, dtype=float)
    return np.concatenate((xi.T.reshape(-1), eta.T.reshape(-1)))


def apply_potential_blocks(potential_blocks, xi, eta, radial_grid, mode_table):
    """Apply the TERPSICHORE potential block operator without dense assembly."""

    xi = np.asarray(xi, dtype=float)
    eta = np.asarray(eta, dtype=float)
    lmns = mode_table.size
    n_intervals = radial_grid.n_intervals
    if xi.shape != (lmns, n_intervals + 1):
        raise ValueError(f"xi must have shape {(lmns, n_intervals + 1)}, got {xi.shape}.")
    if eta.shape != (lmns, n_intervals):
        raise ValueError(f"eta must have shape {(lmns, n_intervals)}, got {eta.shape}.")
    out_xi = np.zeros_like(xi)
    out_eta = np.zeros_like(eta)
    for interval in range(n_intervals):
        x0 = xi[:, interval]
        x1 = xi[:, interval + 1]
        e = eta[:, interval]
        BU = potential_blocks.BU[:, :, interval]
        EI = potential_blocks.EI[:, :, interval]
        CC = potential_blocks.CC[:, :, interval]
        FI = potential_blocks.FI[:, :, interval]
        DI = potential_blocks.DI[:, :, interval]
        GI = potential_blocks.GI[:, :, interval]
        AI = potential_blocks.AI[:, :, interval]
        HI = potential_blocks.HI[:, :, interval]
        BL = potential_blocks.BL[:, :, interval]
        out_xi[:, interval] += BU @ x0
        out_xi[:, interval] += 0.5 * (EI + FI.T) @ e
        out_xi[:, interval] += 0.5 * (CC + AI.T) @ x1
        out_eta[:, interval] += 0.5 * (FI + EI.T) @ x0
        out_eta[:, interval] += DI @ e
        out_eta[:, interval] += 0.5 * (GI + HI.T) @ x1
        out_xi[:, interval + 1] += 0.5 * (AI + CC.T) @ x0
        out_xi[:, interval + 1] += 0.5 * (HI + GI.T) @ e
        out_xi[:, interval + 1] += BL @ x1
    return out_xi, out_eta


def apply_kinetic_blocks(kinetic_blocks, xi, eta, radial_grid, mode_table):
    """Apply the TERPSICHORE kinetic block operator without dense assembly."""

    xi = np.asarray(xi, dtype=float)
    eta = np.asarray(eta, dtype=float)
    lmns = mode_table.size
    n_intervals = radial_grid.n_intervals
    if xi.shape != (lmns, n_intervals + 1):
        raise ValueError(f"xi must have shape {(lmns, n_intervals + 1)}, got {xi.shape}.")
    if eta.shape != (lmns, n_intervals):
        raise ValueError(f"eta must have shape {(lmns, n_intervals)}, got {eta.shape}.")
    out_xi = np.zeros_like(xi)
    out_eta = np.zeros_like(eta)
    for interval in range(n_intervals):
        x0 = xi[:, interval]
        x1 = xi[:, interval + 1]
        e = eta[:, interval]
        BE = kinetic_blocks.BE[:, :, interval]
        BC = kinetic_blocks.BC[:, :, interval]
        BF = kinetic_blocks.BF[:, :, interval]
        BD = kinetic_blocks.BD[:, :, interval]
        BG = kinetic_blocks.BG[:, :, interval]
        BA = kinetic_blocks.BA[:, :, interval]
        BH = kinetic_blocks.BH[:, :, interval]
        BB = kinetic_blocks.BB[:, :, interval]
        out_xi[:, interval] += 0.5 * (BE + BF.T) @ e
        out_xi[:, interval] += 0.5 * (BC + BA.T) @ x1
        out_eta[:, interval] += 0.5 * (BF + BE.T) @ x0
        out_eta[:, interval] += BD @ e
        out_eta[:, interval] += 0.5 * (BG + BH.T) @ x1
        out_xi[:, interval + 1] += 0.5 * (BA + BC.T) @ x0
        out_xi[:, interval + 1] += 0.5 * (BH + BG.T) @ e
        out_xi[:, interval + 1] += BB @ x1
    return out_xi, out_eta


def block_rayleigh_diagnostics(potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, xi, eta, radial_grid, mode_table):
    """Return Rayleigh quotient and generalized residual for a block vector."""

    xi = np.asarray(xi, dtype=float)
    eta = np.asarray(eta, dtype=float)
    k_xi, k_eta = apply_potential_blocks(potential_blocks, xi, eta, radial_grid, mode_table)
    m_xi, m_eta = apply_kinetic_blocks(kinetic_blocks, xi, eta, radial_grid, mode_table)
    vector = pack_global_vector(xi, eta)
    k_vector = pack_global_vector(k_xi, k_eta)
    m_vector = pack_global_vector(m_xi, m_eta)
    wp = float(vector @ k_vector)
    wk = float(vector @ m_vector)
    omega2 = wp / wk
    residual = k_vector - omega2 * m_vector
    residual_norm = float(np.linalg.norm(residual))
    scale = float(np.linalg.norm(k_vector) + abs(omega2) * np.linalg.norm(m_vector))
    relative_residual_norm = residual_norm / scale if scale else 0.0
    return {
        "wp": wp,
        "wk": wk,
        "omega2": omega2,
        "residual_norm": residual_norm,
        "relative_residual_norm": relative_residual_norm,
        "k_vector_norm": float(np.linalg.norm(k_vector)),
        "m_vector_norm": float(np.linalg.norm(m_vector)),
    }

import os

import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - the benchmark runtime is Linux
    fcntl = None


TASK_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SOURCE = TASK_DIR / "source"
if str(SOURCE) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(SOURCE))

SCHEMA_VERSION = "0.4"
SUCCESS_STATUSES = {"workflow_completed", "unsupported"}


def _utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _runner_failure(exc: BaseException) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "status": "runner_failure",
        "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
        "message": str(exc),
    }


def _scientific_failure(reason: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "status": "pre_fix_expected_failure",
        "reason": reason,
    }


def _strict_json(value: object) -> str:
    return json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False)


@contextmanager
def _output_lock(output_dir: Path):
    """Serialize public reproductions that share the task output directory."""
    output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    lock_path = output_dir / "public_multi_equilibrium.lock"
    with lock_path.open("a+", encoding="utf-8") as lock_handle:
        if fcntl is not None:
            fcntl.flock(lock_handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            if fcntl is not None:
                fcntl.flock(lock_handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)


def _atomic_write(path: Path, content: str) -> None:
    """Publish a complete file without exposing a partially written report."""
    temporary_path = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
            mode="w",
            encoding="utf-8",
            dir=path.parent,
            prefix=f".{path.name}.",
            suffix=".tmp",
            delete=False,
        ) as handle:
            temporary_path = Path(handle.name)
            handle.write(content)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary_path, path)
    finally:
        if temporary_path is not None and temporary_path.exists():
            temporary_path.unlink()

    from netCDF4 import Dataset

            M=min(3, metadata["mpol"] - 1),
            N=min(2, metadata["ntor"]),
        )
        grid = LinearGrid(
            rho=np.array([0.5, 0.75, 1.0]),
            M=max(6, min(8, int(eq.M_grid))),
            N=max(1, min(4, int(eq.N_grid))),
            NFP=eq.NFP,
            sym=eq.sym,
        )
        native = terpsichore_native(
            eq,
            grid=grid,
            mode_family=-1,
            M_max=1,
            N_min=-1 if eq.NFP > 1 else 0,
            N_max=1 if eq.NFP > 1 else 0,
            surfs=3,
            ivac=0,
            solver="scipy",
            auto_coefficients=True,
            strict_geometry=True,
            nj=max(8, 2 * int(grid.M) + 1),
            nk=max(1, 2 * int(grid.N) + 1),
        )
        omega2 = float(native.omega2)
        growth_rate = float(native.growth_rate)
        if not (math.isfinite(omega2) and math.isfinite(growth_rate)):
            report.update(
                _scientific_failure(
                    "candidate native scientific chain returned non-finite stability observations"
                )
            )
            report["elapsed_sec"] = time.monotonic() - started
            return report
        report["status"] = "workflow_completed"
        report["observations"] = {
            "omega2": omega2,
            "growth_rate": growth_rate,
        }
    except Exception:
        report.update(
            _scientific_failure("candidate native scientific chain did not complete")
        )
    report["elapsed_sec"] = time.monotonic() - started
    return report


def _write_outputs(payload: dict[str, object], output_dir: Path) -> None:
    report_path = output_dir / "public_multi_equilibrium_report.json"
    summary_path = output_dir / "public_multi_equilibrium_summary.txt"
    report_text = _strict_json(payload) + "\n"
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"run_id: {payload['run_id']}")
    lines.append(f"status: {payload['status']}")
    lines.append(f"started_at: {payload['started_at']}")
    if "completed_at" in payload:
        lines.append(f"completed_at: {payload['completed_at']}")
    lines.append("")
    for case in payload["cases"]:
        lines.append(f"case: {case['case']}")
        lines.append(f"status: {case['status']}")
        lines.append(f"elapsed_sec: {case.get('elapsed_sec', 0.0):.3f}")
        if "error_type" in case:
            lines.append(f"error_type: {case['error_type']}")
        if "reason" in case:
            lines.append(f"reason: {case['reason']}")
        lines.append("")
    _atomic_write(report_path, report_text)
    _atomic_write(summary_path, "\n".join(lines))


def _result_exit_code(payload: dict[str, object]) -> int:
    statuses = {case["status"] for case in payload["cases"]}
    if "runner_failure" in statuses:
        return 2
    if statuses.issubset(SUCCESS_STATUSES):
        return 0
    return 1


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check",
        action="store_true",
        help="compatibility flag; the exit code always reflects the scientific result",
    )
    parser.parse_args()
    cases = (
        ("C0", TASK_DIR / "fixtures" / "public" / "dshape_control" / "wout.nc"),
        ("C1", TASK_DIR / "fixtures" / "public" / "heliotron_primary" / "wout.nc"),
    )
    output_dir = TASK_DIR / "outputs"
    run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    started_at = _utc_now()
    with _output_lock(output_dir):
        _write_outputs(
            {
                "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
                "run_id": run_id,
                "status": "running",
                "started_at": started_at,
                "pid": os.getpid(),
                "cases": [],
            },
            output_dir,
        )
        payload = {
            "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
            "run_id": run_id,
            "status": "running",
            "started_at": started_at,
            "pid": os.getpid(),
            "cases": [_run_case(*case) for case in cases],
        }
        exit_code = _result_exit_code(payload)
        payload["status"] = (
            "passed"
            if exit_code == 0
            else "runner_failure"
            if exit_code == 2
            else "failed"
        )
        payload["completed_at"] = _utc_now()
        _write_outputs(payload, output_dir)
    print(_strict_json(payload))
    return exit_code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Complete the implementation so that supported stellarator-symmetric equilibria

Your implementation will be evaluated on additional equilibria, resolution and

- silently discard asymmetric Fourier content;
